display.title: Episode 494: The Lost Prince (Selichos)
display.summary_short: Late Elul 5751, the week of the first Selichos: a prince returns home in rags and is recognized only by his voice, a parable for 'Shema Koleinu'. Plus Shema with a yeshiva boy.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi greets everyone with ksivah vachasimah tovah as Rosh Hashanah approaches and leads the first Hakochainik march after the summer. Story time is 'The Return of Yisroel'. A king raises his only son with the finest teachers, then sends him out to tour the country, warning him to keep away from dishonest people. Little by little the prince falls in with a bad crowd, copying their speech, dress and ways, until he looks like a tramp. He decides to go home, but how will he prove he is the king's son? The story pauses while a nine-year-old yeshiva boy leads the Shema, followed by tzedakah. At the palace gate the guard laughs at him, and even the king, looking down from the balcony, does not recognize him. Then the boy cries out, 'My father, my king, listen to my voice!' and the king rushes down to embrace him. Uncle Yossi explains that this is what Selichos is about: our wrongdoings have soiled our appearance, but we ask Hashem, Shema Koleinu, to hear our voice. The show ends with candle-lighting time and an invitation to write in about the first night of Selichos in shul.
display.lesson: Even when our deeds have soiled us, we can return to Hashem; He recognizes the genuine voice of His child who comes back in teshuvah.

date.note: First Selichos 'this coming Shabbos night' (Motzei Shabbos 31 Aug 1991, before Rosh Hashanah 5752 on Mon 9 Sep); candles 7:13 fits Friday 30 Aug; one week after ep. 493.
